summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate (Rochester Institute of Technology) building real-time embedded perception systems for autonomous platforms. Optimized GPU inference (TensorRT, CUDA) for object detection, tracking, and segmentation pipelines deployed via embedded software development on Jetson-class edge hardware, including a closed-loop autonomous-driving (ADAS) perception and control stack in CARLA with lane detection and semantic segmentation. Comfortable writing production C++ across embedded and GPU-accelerated systems.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT (OCR-free visual document understanding transformer) on a custom medical billing dataset for structured field extraction.
Built preprocessing and training pipelines in PyTorch using HuggingFace VisionEncoderDecoder API; added domain-specific special tokens and resized decoder embedding layer accordingly.
Improved validation accuracy from 55% to 93% via improved preprocessing and model tuning.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Curated and annotated a custom object detection dataset and trained YOLOv8n, achieving 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation.
Exported the trained model to ONNX and TFLite for embedded/mobile deployment.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed embedded software for a wearable gesture-recognition device, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and Bluetooth to output HID commands via Python.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Trained YOLO11n (mAP50~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD (ResNet-18) for lane detection; integrated into an ADAS-style perception and control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback.

Built automated data-generation pipelines using CARLA's semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering to produce ~5,000 object-detection and ~3,000 lane-tracking training frames with zero manual annotation.
Validated in Town02 with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians; achieved zero collisions and correct traffic-light compliance across multiple laps.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO object detection (5.2x GPU-inference speedup: 56.7->10.9 ms, 17.6->92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) for visual servoing on NVIDIA Jetson embedded hardware.

Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) through systematic unit/integration testing; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects in real time, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
